body: Wilber Rafael Garces Perez, a Venezuelan national living in Austin, is scheduled to appear in federal court in San Antonio on Wednesday for a hearing on his detention. Garces Perez was shot by an ICE officer on September 20 and remains in custody at the South Texas ICE Processing Center in Pearsall. His attorneys are seeking his release, citing his ongoing pain and the need for surgery due to a fractured clavicle and a bullet lodged in his back.

His legal team has expressed concerns about potential infection and permanent damage if he does not receive adequate medical care. Garces Perez was discharged from an Austin hospital to ICE custody following the shooting. His attorneys have questioned the medical treatment he received post-shooting, a claim ICE disputes.

The incident occurred while Garces Perez was working as a DoorDash driver. Austin police reviewed video footage showing a vehicle pursuit before the shooting. Garces Perez stated he was attempting to find a safe location to pull over, while the Department of Homeland Security maintains he tried to evade arrest.

The shooting and Garces Perez's subsequent detention have led to protests in Austin and outside the detention center in Pearsall. His attorney has requested supporters refrain from gathering at the courthouse during the hearing to maintain decorum.
Garces Perez's attorneys are also warning the public about fraudulent online fundraisers, stating that the only authorized fundraiser is through the Austin Sanctuary Network.

attribution.originalTitle: Austin man shot by ICE still in pain, bullet lodged in his back, ahead of San Antonio hearing

faqs.question: What is the current condition of Wilber Rafael Garces Perez?
faqs.answer: Wilber Rafael Garces Perez is experiencing significant pain, has a fractured clavicle, limited mobility, and still has a bullet lodged in his back.

faqs.question: Why is Wilber Rafael Garces Perez in federal court?
faqs.answer: He is in federal court for a habeas hearing where his attorneys are seeking his release from ICE detention.

articles.headline: Houston ISD student dead following shooting outside Westbury High School

articles.takeaway: Sarah Grunau/HPMWestbury High School, where a 17-year-old was shot and killed on Sept.
body: Sarah Grunau/HPMWestbury High School, where a 17-year-old was shot and killed on Sept. 25, 2026. A 17-year-old Westbury High School student was shot and killed near the Houston ISD campus Friday morning, according to the Houston Police Department.

According to police, the shooting occurred at approximately 8:21 a.m. at the end of Dryad Street near Westbury High School in southwest Houston. HPD police Chief Noe Diaz said the shooting happened in an area where students reportedly gather before school every morning.

"Someone came out of a wooded area nearby at a nearby [apartment] complex and from that we believe some words were exchanged and someone produced a handgun and unfortunately someone lost their life as a result of what I call a cowardly act," Diaz said during a press conference Friday morning.

Sign up for the Hello, Houston! daily newsletter to get local reports like this delivered directly to your inbox. In an email, the press office for the Houston Independent School District said the high school was operating in "Secure" mode "while HPD investigates an incident in the area." The victim had not yet been identified, but police confirmed he was a 17-year-old senior of Westbury High School.

As of Friday morning, a suspect was not in custody, but Diaz said investigators "have an idea of who we're looking for." According to police, the high school was not placed in lockdown, and classes had resumed.

Diaz said the Texas Department of Public Safety was assisting with the investigation. This is the second shooting near a Houston-area school this week after a 14-year-old was arrested Wednesday after a 15-year-old was shot and killed outside a Spring ISD high school.

articles.headline: The Austin ICE shooting has raised questions about medical standards for detainees
articles.dek: Wilber Garces Perez was taken to Dell Seton Medical Center on Sunday after being shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent. (Michael Minasi) The recent shooting of a man by an Immigration and Customs Enforcem…
articles.lead: Wilber Garces Perez was taken to Dell Seton Medical Center on Sunday after being shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent. (Michael Minasi) The recent shooting of a man by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer in Austin has led to questions about hospitals’ legal obligations when treating ICE detainees with traumatic injuries.
articles.takeaway: Wilber Garces Perez was taken to Dell Seton Medical Center on Sunday after being shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent.
body: Wilber Garces Perez was taken to Dell Seton Medical Center on Sunday after being shot by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent. (Michael Minasi) The recent shooting of a man by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer in Austin has led to questions about hospitals’ legal obligations when treating ICE detainees with traumatic injuries.
28-year-old Wilber Garces Perez was shot in the back by an ICE officer Sunday. Video shared by the Austin Police Department suggests the shooting followed a car pursuit.

Garces Perez and his lawyer have described an unprovoked encounter with authorities, but the Department of Homeland Services said he was the subject of a “targeted vehicle stop” and attempted to evade arrest.

After the incident, Garces Perez was taken to Austin’s Dell Seton Medical Center for treatment — but he and his lawyer have said they do not believe he was given appropriate care at the hospital, and remains in poor condition at a detention center in South Texas with a bullet still lodged in his back.

Representatives for the hospital and for ICE have disputed the claim that Garces Perez has not received adequate care. But community members and elected officials are still pushing for answers on whether Garces Perez is getting what he needs.

“I am making it very clear to every part of the federal government that ICE needs to take the medical care of Wilber Garces Perez extremely seriously,” Texas Congressman Greg Casar said at a news conference Wednesday.
